title: Why engineers start their careers in Germany
description: What makes Germany a natural choice for engineering students: the universities, the industries that hire, the fields in demand and the myths worth ignoring.
html:
Germany's reputation rests on engineering, and the reputation is deserved. The country trains engineers at a high standard, charges them little or nothing for it and then hires them. If you are considering an engineering degree abroad, here is why Germany belongs on the list.

The universities

The nine large technical universities, along with dozens of universities of applied sciences, offer engineering programmes with strong laboratories, mandatory internships and research links to industry. English-taught master's programmes are widespread; bachelor's programmes are mostly in German, with exceptions at universities of applied sciences.

Fields in demand

Mechanical, electrical and automation engineering remain the core. Automotive engineering is changing fast with electrification, which creates demand for battery, power electronics and software skills. Civil engineering and construction are short of people. Renewable energy, environmental engineering and materials science are growing. Almost every engineering field appears on the official shortage list.

Employers

Car makers and their suppliers, industrial conglomerates, machine builders, chemical and pharmaceutical companies, energy firms and a large base of mid-sized specialists spread across the country. Many of the best employers are in smaller cities, which is worth remembering when choosing a university.

Myths and reality

"You need perfect German": you need working German for many companies, but master's programmes and a growing number of employers run in English, and language courses during the degree close the gap. "It is too competitive": admission to master's programmes requires a solid bachelor's grade, but the number of places is large. "Engineering is only for men": the share of women in engineering programmes is rising and universities run active programmes to support it.

How to start

Choose the field, shortlist programmes using the national programme database, check the language requirement, and plan the finances: a Blocked Account with about €11,900 and health insurance are the visa requirements, and they can be set up before the admission letter arrives.

The bottom line

An engineering degree from a German university costs little, is recognised worldwide and comes with an 18-month window to find a job in one of the world's largest engineering economies. Few other destinations offer that combination.
